lesson_title: The R30 Festival Water: Value, Utility and Markets
hook_text: Same bottle. R9 at the café. R30 inside the festival. Nothing changed — except you.
clip_script: One bottle of water: nine rand at the corner café, thirty rand inside the festival grounds on a blazing afternoon. The water is identical. So what changed? YOU changed — hot, dancing, dehydrated, fenced in with no other option. Economists call that satisfaction utility, and its first law is this: utility lives in the person, never in the product. And it cracks a riddle philosophers argued about for centuries: water keeps every human alive and costs next to nothing, while a diamond keeps nobody alive and costs a fortune. Trading-worth runs on SCARCITY. Water flows from taps everywhere — nobody offers much for one more glass. Diamonds are rare — people bid fortunes. Plentiful trades cheap, scarce trades dear. And the festival proves it in reverse: fence the crowd in, and water inside becomes scarce — its price more than triples on the spot.
visual_style: Split frame: café fridge versus festival stand, one bottle glowing under two price tags; a balance scale tipping a water drop against a diamond on a SCARCITY weight; festival fences closing as the price counter climbs.
mood: Playful riddle energy landing on a clean click of insight.
pacing: Quick setup, riddle posed, suspense beat, crisp resolution.
